title: Director, Dental Furniture Operations
text:
At A-dec, we do more than create the highest quality products and services for the dental industry; we strive to deliver a superior employment experience for each of our team members. With an environment that encourages and assists each person in developing to their highest potential, a career at A-dec is incredibly rewarding.

**Overview**
------------

The Director, Dental Furniture Operations provides strategic direction and end-to-end operational oversight for A-dec’s dental furniture value stream at the Newberg campus. The role leads manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, purchasing, and planning for the value stream and is accountable for delivering the dental furniture business plan, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, cost, inventory, and capacity growth. The Director partners with product line leadership and functions across Manufacturing and the enterprise to translate product and demand plans into a scalable, high-mix, engineered-to-order operation, while strengthening woodworking capability and continuous improvement.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:**

* End-to-end performance of the Dental Furniture value stream: safety, quality, on-time delivery, cost, and inventory against the business plan.
* Dental Furniture purchasing and production and materials planning, including supplier performance, material availability, and inventory levels.
* Capacity, workforce, equipment, and space plans that support Dental Furniture growth and new product introductions.
* Leadership bench strength and succession for all managers and critical roles in assigned areas.

**JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Lead the managers responsible for manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, purchasing, and planning. Define the area’s operating system, including standards, tiered performance reviews, and escalation paths, and hold managers accountable for meeting customer and company safety, quality, delivery, and cost standards.
* Develop annual business plans and budgets, including key performance indicators; assess current capacity and capability and establish multi-year plans for workforce, equipment, space, and investment to meet forecasted demand and support growth; prepare business cases for capital and expense needs.
* Set direction for Dental Furniture manufacturing engineering, including process technology, automation, and capital project priorities that improve safety, quality, throughput, and cost and strengthen woodworking capability.
* Own purchasing and production and materials planning for the Dental Furniture line, including supplier selection and performance, material availability, and inventory targets; operate within enterprise purchasing policies, partner with Global Sourcing on commodity strategy and shared suppliers, and represent the value stream in the enterprise SIOP process.
* Partner with product line leadership, Product Development, and Marketing to translate product strategy, roadmap, and pricing into executable operational initiatives and support the transition of new products into production.
* Set annual targets for safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and efficiency; own results and lead monthly operating reviews with managers to set priorities and drive systemic corrective action.
* Lead deployment of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement across assigned areas; set and prioritize the improvement portfolio against the business plan and build a culture of creative problem solving, collaboration, learning, and development.
* Ensure operations within assigned areas comply with company safety, regulatory, and quality policies and applicable environmental requirements; partner with Environmental Health and Safety, Quality, and other functions to address risks and sustain compliance.
* Set performance objectives for direct reports, review results, and hold them accountable for achieving annual business objectives; take appropriate corrective action when needed.
* + Own workforce strategy for assigned areas: with managers, assess capabilities, close skill and staffing gaps, and plan labor against forecasted demand. Develop managers and maintain succession plans for critical roles.
 + Partner with People & Culture to lead organizational design, change management, and employee engagement; promote a respectful, inclusive, and people-focused work environment.
 + Partner with the Director, Manufacturing Operations – Machining & Maintenance on machined-component supply, maintenance service levels, and equipment reliability, and with other Manufacturing leaders on shared capabilities and capital priorities that support Dental Furniture operations.
 + Communicate value-stream priorities, performance, risks, and resource needs to executive leadership, peers, and employees.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Demonstrated ability to lead managers across manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, purchasing, and planning.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, including high-mix, engineered-to-order production and woodworking or related manufacturing processes.
* Ability to develop and execute business plans, budgets, capacity strategies, and capital priorities aligned with product and business goals.
* Understanding of manufacturing engineering, automation, and capital investment planning.
* Ability to interpret operational and financial data and use performance measures to guide decisions that improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and capacity.
* Effective communication, relationship-building, and change leadership skills, including the ability to work across product line leadership, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other functions.
* Ability to manage competing priorities and make timely decisions in a changing manufacturing environment.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing or operations leadership, including at least four years in a senior leadership role.
* Experience leading production planning, materials planning, and purchasing, with accountability for inventory, supplier performance, and SIOP participation.
* Experience leading lean manufacturing and continuous improvement deployment.
* Demonstrated experience leading managers and coordinating multiple functions within a manufacturing value stream.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in business, engineering, operations, or a related field.
* Experience in furniture, woodworking, high-mix, engineered-to-order, or medical device manufacturing.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement certification.

**Physical Requirements:**

Ability to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise maneuver up to 35 pounds with or without assistance on a routine basis. Must have manual hand dexterity to grasp, operate tools and equipment repetitively. Able to walk, stand, sit, bend, reach, and occasionally kneel, climb steps, and twist throughout an entire shift. Some areas may be exposed to chemicals, noise, vibration and /or dust, and require the use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE); such as, but not limited to safety glasses, hearing protection, foot protection, etc.
